profile.stagger_pattern: Council Positions 1, 3, 5, 7 elected in 2015/2019/2023 (terms Jan 1 of following year through Dec 31 four years later). Council Positions 2, 4, 6 and the directly elected Mayor elected in 2017/2021/2025. Mayor's 4-year term runs on the same cycle as Positions 2/4/6. Unexpired-term contests are added to the next odd-year general (e.g. Position 5 in 2021).

tenures.notes: Election to Position 2 sourced high-confidence at https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20171107/King/ ; the 2020-01-13 exit date is the date he assumed the WA House 30th LD seat by appointment, per Wikipedia (secondary source).

Appointed Saturday March 8, 2020 to the seat vacated by Jesse Johnson, on Mayor Ferrell's tie-breaking vote. Ran as 'Gregory Baruso' for Position 2 in the Nov 2, 2021 general and lost to Erica Norton (https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20211102/King/). Seat vacant 2020-01-13 to 2020-03-08.
Elected Nov 2, 2021 (https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20211102/King/). Official city announcement states she 'resigned from Position 2 on May 16, 2023'.

Appointed June 26, 2023; sworn in July 5, 2023 to the remainder of Erica Norton's term (through Dec 31, 2025). Position 2 did not appear on the Nov 2023 ballot because the vacancy arose during/after the May 2023 filing week. Seat vacant 2023-05-16 to 2023-07-05. End date inferred from the term expiry and from Position 2 appearing as a full-term race in Nov 2025; he did not appear as a 2025 candidate.

Same person as the Position 6 holder 2018-2021; returned to council in a different numbered seat after four years off. Confirmed still seated Aug 2026 at https://www.federalwaywa.gov/city-council . Was elected Council President in Jan 2026 and removed from that internal office Feb 10, 2026; he retained the council seat.
Ran unsuccessfully for Mayor in Nov 2025 while retaining Position 3; Washington has no resign-to-run requirement. Council President as of Feb 2026 per https://www.federalwaywa.gov/city-council .

Sworn in Jan 4, 2022 alongside Norton, Walsh and Dovey per Federal Way Mirror (https://www.federalwaymirror.com/news/new-city-council-and-school-board-members-sworn-in/). Did not appear as a candidate in the Nov 2025 Position 4 race; no resignation found.

Re-elected Nov 5, 2019 (high confidence, https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20191105/King/). Resigned to take a job in California; effective date July 31, 2020 per Federal Way Mirror. The July 2020 resignation is corroborated verbatim in the Leandra Craft appointment article ('Mark Koppang, who resigned in July 2020').

Selected Oct 15, 2020 on Mayor Ferrell's deciding vote over Jack Dovey. Article states verbatim 'Her term will run through December 31, 2021.' Ran for the Position 5 unexpired term in the Nov 2, 2021 general and lost to Jack Walsh. Seat vacant 2020-08-01 to 2020-10-15.
Elected to the remainder of Mark Koppang's 2020-2023 term, which had been added to the 2021 general after Koppang's resignation.

Did not appear on the Nov 2021 Position 6 ballot (open contest between Jack Dovey and Renae Seam), and no resignation or appointment for Position 6 was found in 2018-2021. Term-end exit therefore treated as high confidence for the elected term; the precise reason for not seeking re-election is not sourced.
Sworn in Jan 4, 2022. Lost the Nov 4, 2025 Position 6 general to Les Sessoms (https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20251104/King/).
Did not seek re-election in 2019; seat open, won by Linda Kochmar.

Official City of Federal Way biography page lists verbatim 'City Council Deputy Mayor (2018-2019, 2019-2020)'. The Federal Way Mirror appointment article (https://www.federalwaymirror.com/news/councilwoman-susan-honda-appointed-as-federal-ways-deputy-mayor/) states verbatim she 'was appointed from among her fellow council members as the city's next deputy mayor with a 4-3 vote on Tuesday night' and 'was sworn in for the two-year term, replacing Jeanne Burbidge'. That article gives no calendar date (only 'Tuesday night'), so the span is truncated to the panel window start of 2019-01-01 rather than fabricating a January 2018 date. Pre-2022 the internal presiding officer was titled 'deputy mayor'.

Official city biography lists verbatim 'City Council President (2020-2021)'. The presiding-officer title was restyled from deputy mayor to council president for this term; same continuing office. End date is the day before Linda Kochmar was elected council president on 2022-01-04. Wikipedia's Kochmar infobox independently records her as 'Preceded by Susan Honda' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Kochmar). Exact January 2020 start date of the term not retrievable (Laserfiche minutes archive robots-blocked); calendar-year boundary used.

Federal Way Mirror, 2022-01-07: 'The council elected Linda Kochmar as council president.' Vote taken Tuesday, January 4, 2022. At the same meeting a SECOND, subordinate 'deputy mayor' role was newly created and Susan Honda was elected to it ('Susan Honda, former council president, was elected as the deputy mayor and sworn into the role on Tuesday night'); the city bio page records that as 'City Council Deputy Mayor (2022-2023)'. That parallel role is deliberately NOT given its own rows here, because for 2022-2023 the presiding officer of the council was the council president, and recording both would double-occupy this seat.

Federal Way Mirror, 2024-01-02: 'There will be no deputy mayor role on the Federal Way City Council this year.' The council eliminated the subordinate deputy mayor position and re-elected Kochmar as sole council president on a 4-3 vote, leaving one presiding officer from 2024 onward.

LOW CONFIDENCE - CONTINUITY INFERENCE, NOT A DATED RECORD. No January 2025 council reorganization record naming a council president was retrievable: targeted searches for a 2025 reorganization returned nothing, the city's Laserfiche minutes archive at docs.federalwaywa.gov/WebLink is robots-blocked, and the February 2026 coverage of Moore's removal never names his predecessor. Kochmar is carried forward because she was the sourced holder through 2024 and Wikipedia's infobox still showed her 'Assumed office January 4, 2022' with no end date, but the 2025 annual election itself is unsourced. See the matching gaps entry.

Kent Reporter, 2026-02-16: Moore was 'sworn in as a new member of the Federal Way City Council on Jan. 6' and won the council presidency in 'the initial council vote one month ago'; 'After being removed from his position as president of the Federal Way City Council on Feb. 10' he remained 'Councilmember Martin Moore'. exit_mode is recorded as 'unknown' because the actual exit was removal by council vote (the council rescinded the vote that elected him), which is not one of the permitted exit_mode values. He retained his Position 2 council seat throughout; the Position 2 tenure row is unaffected. Corroborated by Federal Way Mirror (https://www.federalwaymirror.com/news/moore-responds-to-dismissal-as-fw-city-council-president/): 'the council voted Feb. 10 to rescind his title as council president.'

Official city biography page heading records verbatim 'Council President - appointed February 2026'. Kent Reporter, 2026-02-16: 'Susan Honda is sworn in as the council president after the vote at the special election on Feb. 10, 2026.' She continues to hold Council Position 3 simultaneously.

run_log.detail: Loaded WebFetch/WebSearch schemas via ToolSearch; confirmed raw/ output directory.

Federal Way: 7 at-large numbered council Positions plus a directly elected strong mayor. Positions 1/3/5/7 on 2015-2019-2023; Positions 2/4/6 plus Mayor on 2017-2021-2025. Covering 2019-2026 requires the 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2025 generals.

Constructed https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/{YYYYMMDD}/King/ for 20171107, 20191105, 20211102, 20231107, 20251104. All five fetched cleanly and returned full Federal Way race lists including the Mayor in 2017/2021/2025.

https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20151103/King/ returned a page containing only Auburn, Bothell, Milton and Pacific city races - Federal Way is absent. Retried the page twice (including a link/pagination inventory: no pagination, no jurisdiction filter) and fetched the linked county export https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20151103/export/20151103_King.csv, which likewise contains no Federal Way rows. The state portal's 2015 King County dataset appears genuinely incomplete for this city, not merely truncated in conversion.

County canvass. A search surfaced the King County official final results PDF for the Nov 3, 2015 general: https://your.kingcounty.gov/elections/2015/nov-general/results/results.pdf . WebFetch could not parse the PDF stream, but the binary was cached locally and pdftotext extracted page 22 verbatim: 'City of Federal Way / Council Position No. 1 Lydia Assefa-Dawson 6,901 53.35% Mark Greene 5,974 46.18% ... Council Position No. 3 Susan Honda 10,734 98.11% ... Council Position No. 5 Julie L. Hiller 5,777 44.08% Mark Koppang 7,287 55.60% ... Council Position No. 7 Dini Duclos 8,748 67.29% P.K. Thumbi 4,197 32.28%'. 2015 cycle resolved at high confidence.

Four mid-term changes found, none of them visible in election results. (1) Jesse Johnson left Position 2 on 2020-01-13 on appointment to the WA House 30th LD. (2) Greg Baruso appointed to Position 2 on 2020-03-08 on Mayor Ferrell's tie-breaking vote. (3) Mark Koppang resigned Position 5 effective 2020-07-31 to take a job in California. (4) Leandra Craft appointed to Position 5 on 2020-10-15, term stated as running through 2021-12-31. Also found: Erica Norton resigned Position 2 on 2023-05-16 mid-meeting, Paul McDaniel appointed 2023-06-26 and sworn in 2023-07-05. Explicit negative sweeps for 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2026 vacancies returned nothing.

Seat count sanity: 7 numbered council positions + 1 directly elected mayor = 8, consistent with Federal Way's mayor-council charter. Present-day roster at https://www.federalwaywa.gov/city-council names Jim Ferrell (Mayor) plus Susan Honda, Lydia Assefa-Dawson, Martin Moore, Melissa Hamilton, Jack Walsh, Les Sessoms and Linda Kochmar - exactly the 7 people the 2023 and 2025 generals predict, closing 2026. Continuity check: Martin A. Moore appears 2018-2021 (Position 6), disappears 2022-2025, reappears 2026 (Position 2) - verified as a genuine four-year absence, not a missed appointment, since the 2021 Position 6 race was an open Dovey/Seam contest and no Position 6 vacancy exists in that window. Homonym check: no surname collisions. Verbatim check: the 2015 names were read from extracted PDF text rather than a model summary.

SCOPE (moved from gaps by ingest): Deputy Mayor / Council President (internal officer title) — Not systematically reconstructed for 2019-2026. Federal Way's council selects an internal presiding officer (styled 'deputy mayor' before 2022, 'council president' from 2022). Only two data points were incidentally sourced: Linda Kochmar elected council president Jan 4, 2022 (Federal Way Mirror), and Martin Moore elected council president Jan 2026 then removed Feb 10, 2026, replaced by Susan Honda (Federal Way Mirror / Kent Reporter / KING 5). This is an internal officer title, not a separate elected seat; every one of the 8 elected seats is fully accounted for. Flagged only for completeness. No tenure rows carry role 'vice_mayor'.
